title: PHP 8. What does this print?
explain: == converts types before it compares. Since PHP 8, "abc" == 0 is false (in PHP 7 it was true). "1" == "01" is true: both strings look like numbers. null == false is true. Use === unless you really want the conversion.

title: What does this print?
explain: After the first loop, $v is still a reference to the last element $a[2]. The second loop writes each value into $a[2]: 1, then 2, then 2 again. Always unset($v) after a foreach by reference.

title: Quantity 0 is a valid value. What does this print?
explain: ?: replaces any 'empty' value (0, '', '0', null, false, []), so 0 becomes 5. ?? replaces only null or a missing value, so 0 stays 0. For form values where 0 is valid, use ??.

title: Money with floats. What does this print?
explain: A float cannot store 0.1 exactly, so 0.1 + 0.2 is 0.30000000000000004 and == 0.3 is false. round() hides it here, but sums of many prices still drift. Store money as integer cents, or use bcmath or a money library.

title: With strict_types. What does this print?
explain: With declare(strict_types=1), PHP does not convert "2" to int for an int parameter. It throws a TypeError. Without strict_types it would silently convert and print 5. Symfony code usually uses strict_types: it finds wrong types early.

title: What does Node print?
explain: map() calls the function with (value, index). So it runs parseInt('1', 0), parseInt('2', 1), parseInt('3', 2). The second argument is the number base: base 1 is invalid, and '3' is not a binary digit. Write .map(Number) or .map(s => parseInt(s, 10)).

title: What does this print?
explain: var has one i for the whole function. The callbacks run after the loop has finished, when i is already 3. With let, every loop step gets its own i, and it prints 0 1 2.

title: What does this print?
explain: + with a string joins strings: "5" + 3 is "53". - works only on numbers, so "5" - 3 is 2. Values from inputs, like $('#qty').val(), are always strings. Convert first: Number(x).

title: What does this print?
explain: == converts types: '' becomes 0, so 0 == '' is true. null == undefined is a special rule: true. === never converts, so null === undefined is false. Use === by default.

title: Symfony 7: how should a controller get the mailer?
explain: Symfony gives services by autowiring: you ask for the interface in the constructor or the action, and Symfony passes the right object. $this->get() does not work for normal services anymore, and new Mailer() skips all configuration.

title: You pushed a commit. Then you ran git commit --amend. What happens on git push?
options: Git deletes the old commit on the server
explain: --amend makes a new commit that replaces the old one. The server still has the old one, so the histories differ and the push is rejected. On your own branch: git push --force-with-lease. On a shared branch: make a new commit instead.

title: What does git pull do?
options: git fetch + merge (or rebase) into your branch
Resets your branch to the server
explain: git pull = git fetch (download) + merge into your current branch. If you want to look first, run git fetch and then git log HEAD..origin/main.

title: https URLs are not detected. Tap the bug.
explain: strpos() returns the position. 'https://' is at the start, so it returns 0, and if (0) is false. It returns false only when the text is missing. Use str_starts_with() (PHP 8), or compare with !== false.

title: /page?id=5 never shows the special page. Tap the bug.
explain: Everything in the query string is a string: '5', not 5. '5' === 5 is false. Use $request->query->getInt('id'), which returns an int.

title: The clicked tab does not become active. Tap the bug.
explain: An arrow function has no own this. this is the outer this (often window), not the clicked tab. Use a normal function, or use the event: $(e.currentTarget).

title: Delete buttons in loaded rows do nothing. Tap the bug.
explain: The click handler is attached when the page loads. The rows come later by AJAX, so their buttons never get a handler. Attach it to a parent that already exists and give a selector: event delegation.

title: TypeError: cannot read 'name' of undefined. Tap the bug.
explain: $.getJSON only starts the request. Line 5 runs at once, before the answer comes, so user is still undefined. Use the data inside the callback, or await the request.

title: The page reloads and 'Sent!' never shows. Tap the bug.
explain: The handler does not stop the normal form submit. The browser sends the form and reloads the page, and the AJAX request can be cancelled. Call e.preventDefault() first.

title: Copilot wrote this login lookup. Tap the bug.
explain: The email goes straight into the SQL text. An input like ' OR '1'='1 changes the query: SQL injection. Send values as parameters, never inside the SQL string.

pr.title: Use DQL for user lookup
pr.author: copilot-fan
pr.body: Copilot suggested a custom query, it looks more flexible.

explain: The email is put inside the DQL text, so DQL injection is possible. findOneBy() was safe: it sends the value as a parameter. If you need a custom query, use the query builder with setParameter().

pr.title: Show line breaks in comments
pr.author: olha-team
pr.body: Users said that new lines in comments are lost.

explain: |raw turns off Twig's escaping. A user can now post
fix:
{{ comment.text|nl2br }}
{# nl2br escapes the text first, then adds
#}

pr.title: Remove custom repository method
pr.author: cleanup-bot
pr.body: findAll() does the same and is simpler.

explain: findAll() loads only orders. The template reads order.customer for every order, and Doctrine runs one extra query each time: 200 orders = 201 queries (N+1). The old method loaded customers with a JOIN.

pr.title: Save each product right away
pr.author: junior-dev
pr.body: So one bad row does not lose all the others.

explain: flush() inside the loop sends one transaction per row: 10,000 rows become 10,000 round trips. Memory also grows, because Doctrine keeps every object. Validate rows before persist, and flush in batches.

pr.title: Simplify password hashing
pr.author: quick-fix
pr.body: Removed the hasher service, md5() is built in.

explain: md5 is fast and has no salt: a leaked database is cracked in minutes. Symfony's password hasher uses bcrypt or argon2 with a salt and is made to be slow. Keep the hasher.
The empty catch hides every error. The user sees 'ok' even when nothing was imported, and nothing is logged. Catch only the error you expect, log it, and tell the user.

Good change. The Request object works in tests and sub-requests, getInt() returns a real int, and 1 is the default when page is missing. Not every PR has a bug: approving good code fast is also a skill.
Good change. Building HTML from strings puts user text in as HTML: XSS. .text() inserts it as plain text, so < and > are shown, not run.

pr.title: Share local config with the team
pr.author: team-player
pr.body: So everyone has the same database password.

explain: .env.local holds passwords and keys. Once committed, everyone with repo access sees them, and they stay in the git history even after you delete the file. Share safe defaults in .env, keep secrets out of git.
fix:
# .gitignore
.env.local
.env.*.local

# safe defaults (no secrets) go in .env
# real secrets: php bin/console secrets:set DATABASE_PASSWORD

title: AI wrote the code: 5 checks before you commit
bullets: Can you explain every line? If not, ask the AI: 'explain this line by line', before you commit.
Inputs: where does each value come from (Request, database, user)? Is it validated?
SQL and HTML: parameters in queries, no |raw in Twig, .text() not .html() for user data.
Errors: what happens when it fails? No empty catch blocks, no 'ok' when it failed.
Run it: try the normal case AND one bad input (empty, too long, wrong type).

title: A Symfony request: who does what
bullets: The Router matches the URL to a controller action (#[Route]).
The controller reads input from Request, calls services, and returns a Response.
Services get what they need by autowiring (constructor arguments). Never new for a service.
Doctrine: an entity is a row, a repository runs queries, flush() saves.
Twig renders HTML and escapes {{ }} output by default.

title: Before you open a PR on Bitbucket
bullets: Update first: git pull (or rebase on main), fix conflicts on your machine.
Read your own diff line by line. Remove dump(), dd() and console.log.
One topic per PR, small. Title + what and why in the description.
Run the tests and php bin/console lint:twig templates/.
